{{Short description|German mathematician and astronomer}}
'''Abdias Treu''' (sometimes spelled '''Trew''') (29 July 1597 – 12 April 1669) was a German mathematician and academic. He was the professor of mathematics and physical science at the [[University of Altdorf]] from 1636-1669. He is best known for his contributions to the field of [[astronomy]].<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MyZVAAAAYAAJ&q=%22abdias+treu%22+%221597%22|title=The British Library Journal|volume=1-3|year=1975|page=62|last1=Library|first1=British}}</ref> He also contributed writings on the mathematical nature of [[music theory]].<ref>{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=axgrBgAAQBAJ&q=%22abdias+treu%22+%22music%22&pg=PA175|title=Number to Sound: The Musical Way to the Scientific Revolution|author= Paolo Gozza|page=175|year=2013|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=9789401595780}}</ref> He is the grandfather of physician and botanist [[:de:Christoph Jacob Trew|Christoph Jacob Treu]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Die Fruchtbringende Gesellschaft unter Herzog August von Sachsen-Weissenfels|author=Martin Bircher|publisher=Fruchtbringende Gesellschaft, Kommission M. Niemeyer|year=1997|page=57}}</ref>
